lang_en:
One October night, every stall on that street grilled the same skewers, and Zoya was starving.
She wanted the first free bench, and I wanted one good reason.
She sat at the nearest stall while I was deciding.
I asked for one minute, and she started counting out loud.
So I stood in the smoke, looking for a story.
NakshIQ had one, among the oldest skewer shops on the chowk, roasting mutton seekh over charcoal.
Its tip said order by the dozen, chutneys and all, and on Srinagar's Khayam Chowk, Zoya ate more than me.
Travel intelligence is knowing which smoke to follow.
NakshIQ.
lang_hi:
अक्टूबर की एक रात, उस गली की हर दुकान पर एक जैसी सीख़ें सिक रही थीं, और ज़ोया को ज़ोर की भूख लगी थी।
उसे बस पहली खाली बेंच चाहिए थी, और मुझे कोई एक ठीक वजह।
मैं सोच ही रहा था कि वो सबसे पास वाली दुकान पर जाकर बैठ गई।
मैंने एक मिनट माँगा, और वो ज़ोर ज़ोर से गिनती गिनने लगी।
तो मैं धुएँ में खड़ा होकर कोई कहानी ढूँढने लगा।
NakshIQ पर मिली, इस चौक की सबसे पुरानी सीख़ वाली दुकानों में एक, जहाँ कोयले पर मटन सीख़ सिकती है।
टिप थी कि दर्जन के हिसाब से मँगाओ और चटनियाँ मत छोड़ो, और श्रीनगर के ख़य्याम चौक पर ज़ोया ने मुझसे ज़्यादा खाया।
ट्रैवल इंटेलिजेंस है ये जानना कि किस धुएँ के पीछे जाना है।
NakshIQ.

shots: Night, close on a long open-air charcoal grill: rows of metal skewers of minced mutton over glowing coals, thick smoke rising under a bare bulb, no people, no readable signage.

Wide shot from behind at night: two friends in their late 20s, a man and a woman, stand still side by side in a narrow street lined with lit open-air barbecue stalls, smoke drifting under bare bulbs, both already in frame, nobody else, no readable signage.

Medium shot from the side at night: the woman sits on a plain wooden bench at the nearest stall with her hands resting in her lap, the man standing a step behind her, both faces turned away from camera, charcoal glow beside them.
Wide from behind at night: the man stands alone and still in drifting grill smoke between two lit stalls, holding his phone low with the screen turned away from camera.

Close at night on a wooden counter: one steel plate holding a row of charcoal-roasted mutton seekh kebabs and one folded flatbread, beside three small steel bowls of green, pale brown and red chutney, smoke drifting across, no hands, no people.

Wide at night: the two friends sit side by side on the wooden bench at the stall counter, between them one steel plate with only a single kebab left and the three chutney bowls, the woman's hand resting on the counter beside the plate, charcoal glow and smoke behind them, both faces turned away, nobody else in frame.
